nodes.content: Design an incremental cross-module optimizer that preserves optimization benefits while maintaining sound cache reuse under symbol interposition.
requirements: Match clean-build semantics under dependency changes, dynamic symbol interposition, and mixed optimized/unoptimized modules.
For single-module edits, halve full-LTO rebuild time while keeping runtime within 5% of full LTO.

nodes.content: Cache ThinLTO imports keyed by transitive fingerprints; optimize only non-preemptible definitions, rebuild affected partitions, and conservatively link unoptimized modules.
Which dependency and symbol-binding changes must invalidate cached imports to preserve clean-build behavior under ELF interposition?
Hashing transitive imports and ELF bindings (weak resolution, versions, unoptimized exports), while excluding preemptible symbols, matches clean-build semantics.
Implement binding-aware keys; differential-test interposition, weak/versioned symbols, dependency edits, and mixed modules against clean builds; measure rebuild time and runtime.
Run ELF-Interpose-80 cached-versus-clean builds across weak/versioned exports, LD_PRELOAD, dependency edits, and native objects; compare runtime traces and symbol bindings.
ELF-Interpose-80: 3/80 cached links failed after native objects referenced previously pruned exports; import and definition-binding hashes remained unchanged.
Hash native undefined-symbol sets into binding-aware keys and retain referenced exports; cached links should match clean builds on ELF-Interpose-80.
Rerun ELF-Interpose-80 with native undefined-symbol keys and export retention; compare cached and clean link outcomes, bindings, and traces.
ELF-Interpose-80: 80/80 cached builds matched clean link outcomes, symbol bindings, and runtime traces; three missing exports restored.
Adopt native undefined-symbol keys and export retention: they address the three missing-export failures and passed all 80 clean-build comparisons.
Run LTO-Rebuild-30 single-module edits with adopted native-symbol keys; compare rebuild time and SPEC CPU2017 runtime against full LTO.
LTO-Rebuild-30 report containing per-edit rebuild times, cache-hit logs, and SPEC CPU2017 runtime ratios versus full LTO.
Can selective partition rebuilds halve LTO-Rebuild-30 edit latency while keeping SPEC CPU2017 runtime within 5% of full LTO?
Selective partition rebuilds will halve median LTO-Rebuild-30 latency while keeping SPEC CPU2017 slowdown within 5% of full LTO.
Cache per-module specialization recipes, then replay only those whose dependency hashes and final ELF symbol resolutions still match.
Implement resolution-guarded specialization recipes; compare cached and clean builds on ELF-Interpose-80, then benchmark LTO-Rebuild-30 against latency and runtime targets.
Using n11's LTO-Rebuild-30 baseline, benchmark guarded recipe replay's single-module rebuild latency and SPEC CPU2017 runtime against full LTO.
Recipe-Replay-30 report comparing guarded replay with n11’s baseline: median rebuild time, SPEC CPU2017 slowdown, and cache-rejection counts.
Audit Recipe-Replay-30 against 50% latency and 5% slowdown targets; rerun ELF-Interpose-80 with weak bindings and native exports.
Recipe-Replay-30: median rebuild time was 0.64× full LTO, missing the 0.50× target; SPEC CPU2017 slowdown was 3.1%.
Which recipe-replay stage accounts for the 0.14× full-LTO latency gap to the 0.50× target?
Repeated ELF resolution checks account for at least 0.14× full-LTO time; input-keyed resolution-map caching should reach 0.50× rebuild latency.
Profile ELF-resolution overhead on Recipe-Replay-30; cache maps by linker-input fingerprints and rerun rebuild timing plus ELF-Interpose-80 equivalence.
Repeated ELF resolution consumed 0.16× full-LTO time; cached maps achieved 0.48× median rebuild latency and 80/80 ELF-Interpose-80 equivalence.
Adopt resolution-map-cached replay: n22’s 0.48× latency and 80/80 equivalence restore p2’s viability after n18’s latency failure.
Benchmark selective partitions versus resolution-map-cached replay using n11’s LTO-Rebuild-30 baseline; measure SPEC CPU2017 runtime and ELF-Interpose-80 equivalence.
LTO-Rebuild-30: selective partitions took 0.58× full-LTO time; cached replay took 0.48×, with 3.1% SPEC CPU2017 slowdown and 80/80 interposition equivalence.
Reoptimize affected hot call-graph components incrementally, preserving indirect calls to preemptible symbols and exports referenced by native objects.
How should edited hot call-graph components expand to retain cross-module inlining benefits without reoptimizing unaffected components?
Using n11’s baseline, benchmark 0–2-hop hot-component expansion against p1’s import caching on rebuild time, SPEC slowdown, and interposition equivalence.
LTO-Rebuild-30: import-cached partitions took 0.58× full-LTO time; one-hop components took 0.46×, with 2.8% SPEC slowdown and 80/80 interposition equivalence.
Does one-hop expansion sustain 0.46× rebuild latency and ≤5% SPEC slowdown on high-fanout dependency edits?
For edits affecting ≥20 hot callers, one-hop expansion retains ≤0.50× full-LTO rebuild time and ≤5% SPEC CPU2017 slowdown.
Construct Fanout-24 edits affecting ≥20 hot callers; measure one-hop rebuild latency, SPEC CPU2017 slowdown, and clean-build equivalence.
Run Fanout-24 one-hop and import-cache builds against n11’s baseline; measure rebuild latency, SPEC CPU2017 slowdown, and clean-build equivalence.
Fanout-24: one-hop reached 0.49× full-LTO time and 4.2% SPEC slowdown; import caching reached 0.57×; both matched 24/24 clean builds.
Expand Fanout-24’s passing cases to ≥40 hot callers with LD_PRELOAD and native objects; remeasure one-hop latency, SPEC slowdown, and equivalence.
Fanout-24 ≥40-caller cases: one-hop rebuilds took 0.50× full-LTO time, incurred 4.7% SPEC slowdown, and matched 24/24 interposed clean builds.
Adopt one-hop hot-component rebuilds over import caching: 0.46–0.50× latency, ≤4.7% slowdown, and clean-build equivalence across both benchmarks.
When must a cached hot component be invalidated after weak-symbol resolution, symbol-version, or native-object dependency changes?
Extend n16’s replay cases with weak-resolution, version, and native-reference changes; compare recipe and component invalidation against clean builds.
Binding-Delta-48: guarded recipes matched 48/48 clean builds; hot-component caching reused stale inlining in two default-version switches.
Guard one-hop hot-component caches with input-keyed ELF binding maps and native-reference fingerprints, invalidating affected components before reuse.
Which ELF binding and native-reference changes require one-hop cache invalidation without losing the 0.50× rebuild target?
Input-keyed checks of weak bindings, default versions, and native references should achieve 48/48 clean-build equivalence at ≤0.50× full-LTO latency.
Implement binding-map invalidation for version, weak, and native-reference deltas; rerun Binding-Delta-48 and Fanout-24 with cold and warm caches.
Implement one-hop binding-map invalidation; compare Binding-Delta-48 cache rejections with n16’s report and Fanout-24 timings with n11’s baseline.
Guarded-Components report with Binding-Delta-48 invalidation logs, Fanout-24 rebuild-time ratios, and clean-build binding and trace comparisons.
Audit Guarded-Components for 48/48 clean-build equivalence, ≤0.50× Fanout-24 rebuild latency, and ≤5% SPEC CPU2017 slowdown.
Guarded-Components matched 48/48 clean builds, but Fanout-24 median rebuild time rose to 0.56× full LTO.
Invalidate only components recording changed symbol bindings; shared resolution-map caching should restore ≤0.50× latency while preserving 48/48 equivalence.
Use Guarded-Components logs to implement binding-use invalidation and shared resolution maps; retest 48/48 equivalence and ≤0.50× Fanout-24 latency.
Binding-use invalidation achieved 48/48 clean-build equivalence and reduced Fanout-24 median rebuild time from 0.56× to 0.49× full LTO.
Compare n49’s guarded components with n33’s import caching on Fanout-24 and Binding-Delta-48 for latency, slowdown, and equivalence.
Fanout-24: guarded components took 0.49× versus import caching’s 0.57× full-LTO time, with 4.7% slowdown and 48/48 Binding-Delta equivalence.
Adopt binding-use-guarded one-hop components: fix version-switch staleness and 0.56× regression; achieve 0.49× latency, 4.7% slowdown, 48/48 equivalence.
Integrate n52’s guarded components using n44 logs; verify clean-build equivalence under dependency edits, interposition, and mixed modules, then benchmark targets.
Incremental-LTO v1 patchset with binding-use-guarded one-hop caches, native-export retention, resolution-map fingerprints, and clean-build and performance regression tests.
